title.en: Khushwant Singh and the grandmother's portrait

heading.en: A grandmother who was always old

hook.en: Can you imagine your grandmother as a little girl? The author could not. To him she had always been old, wrinkled and quietly beautiful.

objectives.en: Introduce Khushwant Singh and the form of the piece
Describe the grandmother's appearance and nature
Explain why the author found it hard to imagine her young

narration.en: Can you imagine your grandmother as a little girl? The author could not. To him she had always been old, wrinkled and quietly beautiful.

body.en: Khushwant Singh (1915–2014) was a well-known Indian journalist, historian and novelist, admired for his wit and frank style. "The Portrait of a Lady" is an autobiographical pen-portrait of his grandmother. He traces their relationship through three stages of his own life: childhood in the village, school years in the city, and his years at university and abroad.

narration.en: Khushwant Singh (1915–2014) was a well-known Indian journalist, historian and novelist, admired for his wit and frank style. "The Portrait of a Lady" is an autobiographical pen-portrait of his grandmother. He traces their relationship through three stages of his own life: childhood in the village, school years in the city, and his years at university and abroad.
Let us map the grandmother's portrait: her looks, her faith and the people around her.

say.en: At the centre of the piece is the author's grandmother, a deeply religious woman.
She was short, plump and slightly bent, with silvery white hair.
Her lips moved in prayer and her fingers told her rosary beads.
The grandfather is known to the author only through a portrait on the wall.
She feeds the village dogs and, later, the city sparrows.
The narrator is her grandson, who grew up in her care.
She always dressed in spotless white, which suits her calm spirit.

narration.en: The author traces his bond with his grandmother through three stages of his life. Sort each memory.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಕಾರ್ಡನ್ನು ಓದಿ, ಅದು ಸೇರುವ ಗುಂಪಿಗೆ ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ.

prompt.en: Sort each memory into Village, City school or University years.

text.en: She walks him to the temple school
They feed stale chapatis to the village dogs
He goes to school by motor bus
She cannot help with English or science lessons
She is upset that he is taught music
He is given a room of his own
She feeds the sparrows in the courtyard every afternoon

explanation.en: Each stage loosens their daily companionship, yet her love and dignity stay the same.

body.en: For as long as the author could remember, his grandmother had been old and wrinkled, and stories of her as a pretty young girl sounded like fairy tales to him. She was short, plump and slightly bent, with silvery white hair, and she dressed in spotless white. She hobbled about the house with one hand on her waist, while the other hand told the beads of her rosary and her lips moved in silent prayer. The author compares her calm, white presence to a peaceful winter landscape in the mountains: to him she was not pretty, but beautiful.

points.en: Appearance: short, plump, slightly bent, white hair
Always praying and telling her rosary beads
Image: serene like a snowy mountain landscape
Her beauty is inner beauty: peace and contentment

problem.en: Why did the author find it hard to believe that his grandmother had once been young and pretty?

steps.en: For twenty years he had seen her looking exactly the same: old and wrinkled.
Stories about her childhood games sounded to him like fairy tales.
Even the grandfather's portrait made it hard to picture them young.

answer.en: The author had known his grandmother only as an old, wrinkled woman who never seemed to change. Stories of her as a pretty young girl playing games felt like fairy tales, so he could not imagine that she had ever been young.

points.en: Khushwant Singh draws a loving pen-portrait of his grandmother.
She was old, short, slightly bent, white-haired and always at prayer.
Her beauty was the beauty of peace and contentment, not of looks.

homework.en: Write a 100-word description of an elderly person you admire, focusing on inner qualities.
